blocks.text: Status: CANONICAL — CONTROLLED-ENGLISH GATE MAY BEGIN

The renderer accepts only canonical EZIR-JSON-1 semantic IR with a valid content-derived UTT identity. It resolves every lexical target against the 324 canonical atoms or 28 approved compounds, preserves the exact semantic graph, and emits an EZF-1 document containing the complete source IR plus a deterministic performance plan and diagnostic literal gloss.

Lexical generation emits the fixed family-qualified transliteration, formal carrier, harmonic family opening, and relative note path for every atom. Compounds expand in qualifier-before-head order. Only the semantic head receives the compound occurrence’s runtime ending. Any open compound participant slot—such as the source and target of the directed data-link template—must be explicitly bound by a typed fills_role edge before rendering.

The default middle-register anchor is MIDI 60; anchors from 24 through 96 are valid. Register offsets are low −12, middle 0, high +12, and sustained-background −5 semitones. Exact pitch and reference duration are presentation choices. Meaning is carried by the relative harmonic, address, contour, timing, and register relations, so transposition does not change the UTT identity or EZF identity.

Runtime state [0] descends one semitone from the address-final note and stops sharply. Runtime state [1] returns firmly to the phrase/register starting pitch. Runtime state [2], whose fixed name is num, rises seven semitones—a perfect fifth—from the address-final note and sustains. num is not a numeric parameter.

Primary speech-act contours are level assertion, rising question, sharply falling command, rise-then-return definition, and fall-then-rise possibility. Secondary contours mark repetition, parallelism, and unresolved condition or dependency. Structural timing maps qualification to no gap, role filling to a short gap, ordinary structural edges to a medium gap, parallel membership to overlap, repetition to repeated pulse, and statement completion to a long gap.

Formal identity is the SHA-256 digest of the semantic digest plus the transposition-independent relative performance plan; the visible identifier uses EZF:<first 24 lowercase hexadecimal digits>. The inverse decoder regenerates the expected rendering and rejects mismatches in identity, semantics, generated forms, notes, runtime endings, registers, contours, timing, or gloss. It never guesses or repairs. Successful decoding returns the original canonical semantic IR exactly.

The dedicated validator passes 12 of 12 checks. It proves 48 Semantic-IR round trips across MIDI anchors 48, 60, and 72; 972 exhaustive atom/runtime-state renderings; 84 approved compound/runtime-state renderings; required compound-slot enforcement; exact transposition shifts with invariant relative plans and formal identities; and rejection of corrupted formal documents. The complete project regression also passes every atomic, compound, sense-index, coverage, etymology, Semantic-IR, renderer, and family-soundness check.

This milestone changes no atomic title, invariant definition, address, compact root, carrier, note path, approved compound meaning, or English sense route. Controlled English is the next authorized gate. General-English translation and glyph/audio work remain unauthorized until their preceding gates pass. The controlled-English compiler must map a deliberately bounded input grammar into canonical Semantic IR, then use this renderer and decoder without bypassing semantic validation.
